text.p: Italian bond futures recovered strongly along with other European markets helped by the firmer dollar while operators saw Friday as just a temporary sell-off opportunity, dealers said.
"Friday's fall was held, with U.S. markets recovering late in the day after Europe had closed, so the mood was soon positive across the board today," said one LIFFE trader.

Dealers said the Italian market was helped as Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said Italian CPI was averaging 3.8 percent in 1996 and he added that data in a few weeks time will show whether Italy's CPI is heading in the right direction.

Markets were soothed early as U.S. officials played down comments by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan last week, saying he was just raising a question about the level of the stock market rather than saying it had risen too high.
Dealers added that markets had calmed down from Friday and that Italy was likely to look for its next move from world markets with little domestic news or data seen this week.
The Italian 1997 financial budget for 1997 is set for debate in the full chamber of the upper house Senate from Tuesday, with the final vote in the chamber expected next week.
